about: A saved measurement's own logic — the same cases in every edition. Every case is a classical guitar measurement (guitarType 'Classical', measurementType 'Classical Guitar') holding 'peaks' (id, frequency in Hz, magnitude in dB), the 'selected' peak ids (null: no selection saved — a legacy file; []: Select None) and mode 'overrides' (peak id → label). tapToneRatio: the measurement's ratio, f(Top) / f(Air) over the definitive peaks — 'expect' within 'ratioTolerance', or null for none; 'live' rows are also given to a live analyzer with the same peaks, selection and overrides, which must give the same ratio. modeLabels: the label each peak is written with, in peak order — and the label the measurement gives it for display (the Details pane's), which must be the same; 'storedLabels' are labels the file already carries. selectionHeal: the measurement written and read back — whether the read flags it healed, and the selection it holds; 'material' rows are a material measurement (a longitudinal snapshot, no guitar spectrum). Expected values are Swift's. snapshotBytes: the spectrum written as base64 'frequenciesData' / 'magnitudesData' — exact text — and read back to the same float32 values. decode: a 'file' (the .guitartap array) and the fields it must read to: measurementName, peakMinThreshold, sampleRate (null: unknown), the snapshot's frequencies and magnitudes, overrides (peak id → label, ids compared ignoring case; {} for none), peakCount, the first peak's pitchNote, annotationVisibilityMode; or 'rejected' — the file cannot be read (a measurement with no spectrum: no guitar spectrum, no plate/brace longitudinal one, or a comparison of fewer than two entries — and a spectrum with no points, or with frequencies and magnitudes that differ in number, is no spectrum, a comparison entry's included). write: a 'file' read and written again by the edition's writer — the keys that must be 'present' and 'absent' (a key anywhere in the document; 'peaks[].modeLabel' on every peak), the exact number 'text' written for a key, and text the output 'contains' once compact. fixtures: the real files every edition carries — each read to the facts given (the first measurement's name, peak count, sample rate, whether it is a comparison, its override labels), each override naming a peak the file contains, written again with no legacy key and with the spectrum's 'frequenciesData' / 'magnitudesData' exactly as the file has them, and read back with the same peaks and spectrum. comparison: a 'file' holding a comparison record, read (and, with 'roundTrip', written by the edition's writer and read again); 'expect' — 'isComparison', 'healed' (the reading healed something and flags the record to be saved again), 'entries' (per entry, in order, the fields named: id, label, colorComponents, guitarType — null for none — peakCount, modePeakIds: the stored map, mode display name → peak id, ids compared ignoring case; or null for no entries), 'modeFrequency' (the first entry's stored modes read back as frequencies), 'absent' (keys the written document does not contain). ids: the rule for ids — every id is a UUID (RFC 9562): read in either case and compared as the same id, written uppercase, and a file holding one that is missing or not in the hyphenated 8-4-4-4-12 form cannot be read. A 'file' read by the edition's reader; 'rejected': the reading fails; otherwise 'expect' — 'selectedFrequencies' (the selected peaks, by frequency), 'overrideLabels' (frequency → the mode name on that peak), 'offsets' (frequency → the label position for that peak, [Hz, dB]), 'writtenLowercaseIds' (written again by the edition's writer: how many UUID-form strings in it hold a lowercase letter).

tapToneRatio.note: Air and a Top in the classical Top/Back overlap zone, nothing selected: the Top is found
no Air peak (250 Hz is Back for classical): no ratio
only the selected peaks count: Air and Top selected, a 500 Hz peak not
the Top renamed to a freeform label is no longer the definitive Top: no ratio
an override that makes a peak Top retargets the ratio onto it
a Top that is not selected is not the definitive Top: no ratio
two peaks in the overlap zone: the stronger is Top, and the ratio uses it alone
Select None: nothing is selected, so there is no definitive Air or Top — no ratio

modeLabels.note: two peaks in the overlap zone get distinct labels: the stronger Top, the weaker Back
a stale label carried in the file does not win: the stronger peak, saved as Back, is reclassified
the selection does not change a peak's mode: with Air and 220 Hz selected, 220 Hz is still Back — classified among all the peaks, as the live view did

selectionHeal.note: nothing selected: healed to the definitive set (strongest per mode), flagged, and the ratio is available
two Tops selected (175 and 185 Hz are both Top-only for classical): pruned to the stronger; the Air is untouched
a valid one-per-mode selection is not flagged as healed
a material measurement is never touched by the selection heal
Select None is kept: an empty saved selection is not healed, and reads back as nothing selected
no peaks and no selection saved (a comparison record, or nothing detected): nothing to select, so not healed

snapshotBytes.note: frequencies and magnitudes are written as base64 of little-endian float32 values
an empty spectrum is an empty string

decode.note: the legacy 'tapLocation' key is read as the measurement name
the legacy 'peakThreshold' key is read as Peak Min
a missing sample rate is unknown
a legacy snapshot with plain number arrays
overrides in the legacy object form, keyed by a lowercase peak id
overrides in the current flat form, as Python writes them
an 'auto' override entry means no override and is dropped
a peak without pitch fields has no pitch
a measurement with no spectrum cannot be read: no edition saves one
a guitar measurement's spectrum makes it readable
a plate or brace's spectrum is its longitudinal one: readable without a guitar spectrum
a comparison of one entry cannot be read: comparing takes at least two
an empty spectrum is no spectrum: a measurement whose spectrum has no points cannot be read
frequencies and magnitudes that differ in number are not a spectrum: the measurement cannot be read
a plate/brace whose longitudinal spectrum has no points has no spectrum: it cannot be read
a comparison is its entries' spectra: one with an entry whose spectrum has no points cannot be read

write.note: legacy keys are read, never written back
unset optionals are omitted, not written as null
Float fields are written as their shortest float32 text, not a float64 expansion: the file gives each value as the float64 expansion of a float32
an override is written as an assigned entry with its label

fixtures.note: saved before the findPeaks duplicate fix: one twin peak, dropped on read
saved before the findPeaks duplicate fix: one twin peak, dropped on read
saved before the findPeaks duplicate fix: one twin peak, dropped on read

comparison.note: a comparison record written and read back keeps each entry — id, label, colour, guitar type, peaks and stored modes
an entry with no guitar type is written without one
an entry saved before the stored modes existed is healed by position on reading, and flagged to be saved again
the stored modes are read back as stored — not classified again — even where classification would differ
an ordinary measurement is not a comparison

ids.note: a file whose ids are all lowercase — as Python wrote them before 2026-09-20 — reads with its selection, mode name and label position on their peak, and is written back uppercase
ids that differ only in case still match: lowercase selection and mode-name key against uppercase peak ids, a lowercase measurement id
a measurement id that is not a UUID: the file cannot be read
a measurement with no id: the file cannot be read
a peak id that is not a UUID
a selected peak id that is not a UUID
a plate/brace peak id that is not a UUID
a mode-name key that is not a UUID, in the flat [key, value, …] form
a mode-name key that is not a UUID, in the {key: value} form older writers used
a label-position key that is not a UUID
a label-position key that is not a UUID, its value a legacy form that would itself be dropped: the key is still an id
control: a tap entry with UUIDs reads
a tap entry id that is not a UUID
a tap entry's peak id that is not a UUID
a tap entry's selected peak id that is not a UUID
control: a comparison entry with UUIDs reads
a comparison entry id that is not a UUID
a comparison entry's source measurement id that is not a UUID
a comparison entry's mode peak id that is not a UUID
a comparison entry's peak id that is not a UUID
only the hyphenated 8-4-4-4-12 form is a UUID here, as Swift reads one: in braces it is not
nor without its hyphens
nor as a urn:uuid: name
